(societe en commandite).

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every direct and indirect UBO, general partner, and proposed officer against: (i) UN Consolidated List; (ii) Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, the United Nations Act, and the Criminal Code (terrorist entities); (iii) OFAC SDN list as a market standard given USD Swift/Wire and Standby LC payment rails; and (iv) FINTRAC-aligned politically exposed person (PEP) databases covering both foreign and domestic PEPs. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, senior government official, head of state, or sanctioned-country nexus; results must be recorded in a written AML/CFT risk assessment prior to name approval, registration, or banking onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) — French-language online portal 'Recherches et reservations de noms' at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The enterprise name must be in French under the Charter of the French Language (RLRQ c.C-11). French must be the dominant element of any bilingual legal name; a foreign-language version (e.g., Chinese characters) may be recorded only as a secondary designation after an approved French name. Transliteration from Latin or non-Latin scripts must follow the Registrar's orthographic rules and must not create phonetic confusion with an existing name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Token requiring prior ministerial or AMF approval: 'banque', 'banquier', 'assurance', 'assureur', 'fiduciaire', 'societe de fiducie', 'bourse', 'courtier', 'trust'
Token reserved to recognized professionals: 'avocat', 'notaire', 'comptable professionnel agrege', 'ingenieur', 'medecin', 'architecte'
Token suggesting public or state authority: 'gouvernement', 'ministere', 'municipalite', 'Revenu Quebec', 'Canada', 'Quebec' where it implies sovereign status
Token involving 'administration portuaire', 'garde cotiere', 'port authority', 'coast guard' unless chartered by public statute
Token contrary to public order or morality, or any name creating a likelihood of confusion with an existing enterprise, trademark, or protected legal name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for 90 days and is not extendable; if registration is not completed within the window, a fresh search and new fee payment are required. On rejection, the applicant must, within 30 days of receiving the notice, file a written reconsideration request in French with the Registraire des entreprises, attaching evidence of prior use, trademark protection, or ministerial authorization. If the reconsideration is dismissed, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Court of Quebec (civil chamber) within the statutory appeal period; in the interim, an alternative French language name variant may be reserved to avoid delaying the incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office not accepted as the sole registered office for a Quebec limited partnership. A physical establishment within Quebec, open for service of process and maintenance of corporate records, is mandatory under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and applicable Quebec tax standards; a mail-forwarding address or post-office box alone is insufficient. A registered agent address in Montreal or Quebec City that qualifies as 'adresse de l'etablissement' is permissible, provided it is staffed during ordinary business hours and accessible to public authorities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-high (approximately 30% probability within the first 18 months following registration). The risk is elevated by mandatory GST/QST registration, the medium-risk AML classification of marine bunkering, and the capacity of Revenu Quebec, the Autorite des marches financiers, or FINTRAC to conduct unannounced on-site verifications of commercial substance and records retention.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, Book Five, Title Seven, Arts. 2236-2247 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; the common-law Partnership Act does not apply to Quebec civil-law partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), 455 rue du Parc, Quebec City
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; contributions are governed solely by the limited partnership agreement; no escrow or blocked-account requirement exists under Quebec law, but contributed capital must be fully vested in the partnership before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [NAME] LIMITED PARTNERSHIP. Adopted pursuant to Arts. 2239-2240 of the Civil Code of Quebec. 1. SUBSCRIPTION: The General Partner accepts the agreed capital contributions of the Limited Partners and confirms the issued partnership interests. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The partnership's registered office is established at [ADDRESS], Quebec, and the General Partner is authorized to file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec. 3. APPOINTMENTS: [A] President and [B] Secretary; the President may open bank accounts, sign contracts, and file all tax and licensing applications. Certified as a true copy. General Partner signature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Online Name Reservation Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed name using the mandatory legal element 'Societe en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' via the REQ online portal. The name search verifies conflicts against the Quebec enterprise register and reserved marks. Upon approval, secure the name reservation attestation valid for ninety days.
required_dossiers: Proposed business name containing legal form element
Applicant contact details and email address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, REQ issues a reasoned notice; amend the distinctive component and pay the reduced re-search fee; alternatively, file a written objection to the Registrar within the prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties before a Quebec notary (private writing also permitted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the convention de societe en commandite identifying the general partner's exclusive management power, limited partner capital commitments, profit-sharing formula, and admission/withdrawal rules. Open a partnership bank account with a Schedule I Canadian bank and deposit the initial capital contributions prior to filing for registration.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution records and deposit slips
Certificate and constitutional documents of any corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contractual defects are cured by unanimous written consent or by a supplemental amendment deed; a notarized rectification is executed where a partner's contribution obligation requires third-party reliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Online Entreprise Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the declaration d'immatriculation on the REQ portal, entering the partnership name, Quebec registered office address, full identity of the general partner, and the activity description (NAICS 488390: Other Support Activities for Water Transportation, marine bunkering). Pay the CAD $47.00 filing fee and obtain the enterprise number (NEQ) and registration extract.
required_dossiers: Copy of the executed limited partnership agreement
Proof of registered office address in Quebec
Identification of general and limited partners (name, address, legal nature)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a notice of refusal or request for particulars, respond within thirty days with a corrective declaration and supporting evidence; failure to cure triggers daily late fees and possible cancellation; an administrative review is available before the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Revenu Quebec - Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the federal Business Number through CRA's Business Registration Online and open the relevant program accounts. Where the partnership conducts taxable commercial activity in Quebec, register for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) with Revenu Quebec using the NEQ, and register as an employer with the CNESST and Revenu Quebec payroll accounts if employees are engaged in bunkering operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Quebec denies a requested account, reconcile the partnership's taxable status under the Tax Administration Act and re-file; an appeal may be submitted to the appeals division of the respective agency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preliminary Authorization Consultation for Marine Bunkering Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Transport Canada, Marine Safety and Security Directorate; applicable Canada Port Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-application consultation with Transport Canada Marine Safety to confirm vessel and facility certification pathways under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001. Submit a preliminary safety management plan, fuel transfer procedure, and berth application to the relevant port authority for the intended bunkering site.
required_dossiers: Site plan of the fueling/delivery point
Vessel classification certificates (if bunkering vessels are used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where Transport Canada issues a deficiency notice, submit a corrective action plan within the set deadline and arrange an on-site inspection; refusal may be appealed to the Transportation Appeal Tribunal of Canada.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada, Marine Safety and Security Directorate, in coordination with the applicable Port Authority (e.g., Montreal Port Authority or Quebec Port Authority)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Fuel Bunkering Operating Approval and Vessel Fuel Transfer Permit (certification under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 and applicable port authority by-laws)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Authorization (certificat d'autorisation) under Section 22 of the Environment Quality Act for moderate-risk fuel handling activities; a full environmental impact assessment may be ordered where siting affects riparian zones, protected species, or floodplains, subject to the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL Annex I oil discharge limits (15 ppm effluent standard via oil-water separators) as incorporated by the Canada Shipping Act, 2001; sulphur content limitations under the Sulphur in Marine Fuel Regulations (CEPA 1999) for emission control areas; ISO 8217 marine fuel quality standard; Quebec wastewater effluent discharge criteria under the Règlement sur l'assainissement des eaux; Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 VOC and hazardous air pollutant thresholds for storage tanks and transfer lines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certificate of conformity issued by the local municipal fire safety service for fuel storage and transfer zones; structural and load-inspection certificates by licensed engineers for docks, piers, and bunkering platforms; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance, including a high-risk workplace prevention program; Canadian Coast Guard spill-response readiness validation; workplace hazardous materials information and confined-space safety protocols under the Quebec Act respecting occupational health and safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal GST/HST and income tax administration; Revenu Québec — Quebec QST (TVQ), provincial income tax, and payroll source deductions; Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — enterprise legal registration (NEQ). Corporate/registration portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html), CRA Business Registration Online (BRO), and Revenu Québec's 'Mon Entreprise' portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: If the foreign LP carries on business in Québec, register with the REQ (declaratory registration as an extra-provincial limited partnership under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises) to obtain the NEQ; a Québec-domiciled LP would be constituted by declaration of registration filed with REQ. Step 2: Register with the CRA via Business Registration Online (BRO) or the non-resident business registration procedure to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with GST/HST account (RT prefix); the partnership is a 'person' for GST/HST purposes even though fiscally transparent for income tax. Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec for the QST (TVQ) account (RQ prefix) when the partnership exceeds the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold in Québec or is a GST/HST registrant making taxable supplies in Québec; also open QP payroll account and QD source-deduction account if applicable. Step 4: File partnership information return T5013 and allocate income to partners; non-resident partners' shares of Canadian-source business income are subject to withholding and Part XIII/formatted returns. Step 5: For a partnership with no presence in Canada, CRA still requires a BN and a GST/HST account for any taxable supply activity in Canada; the LP may designate a non-resident agent or use the CRA international tax services office ('Non-Resident' BN registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A Québec limited partnership ('société en commandite' / LP) is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax: no entity-level tax; each partner pays tax on its allocable share (ITA s. 96), and non-resident partners are taxed on Canadian-source shares subject to Part XIII or Part I. For GST/HST and QST, the partnership itself is a separate 'person'/registrant required to register, collect, and remit, with the economic incidence passing through to the partners. There is no corporate 'opaque' default for an LP; however, Canadian anti-hybrid rules may recharacterize arrangements where the jurisdiction of a partner treats the same LP as taxable at entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections relevant to a foreign-owned Québec LP: (i) 'qualifying partnership' GST/HST election under ETA s. 273, and the parallel QST provision, consolidating the partnership and a designated member as a single registrant for filing/ITC purposes; (ii) elective GST/HST and QST registration by a small supplier under ETA s. 240(1) to claim input tax refunds before the mandatory threshold is reached; (iii) non-resident partners' election to be taxed on net Canadian-source income under ITA s. 216 (rental or timber) rather than 25% gross Part XIII withholding; and (iv) no election is available to neutralize hybrid mismatches — ITA s. 18.4 et seq. (enacted 2020) automatically denies deductions or includes amounts where another jurisdiction treats the LP as an opaque entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal VAT) and QST (Québec Sales Tax — VAT-type), administered respectively under the Excise Tax Act (ETA) and the Act respecting the Québec Sales Tax (QSTA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small-supplier threshold). A partnership carrying on business in Canada must register for GST/HST where the value of its worldwide taxable supplies made in Canada exceeds CAD 30,000 in either a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; Quebec's QST threshold mirrors this (CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies made in Québec). Zero-rated supplies generally count toward the threshold; non-residents apply the threshold to their taxable supplies made in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or central invoice pre-clearance exists at the federal level. Invoices under ETA s. 223 must contain prescribed particulars (supplier identity, BN, date, description, tax charged) and may be issued electronically if authentic and legible. Federal GST/HST returns must generally be filed electronically via CRA's GST/HST NETFILE (paper returns restricted); QST returns must be filed electronically via Revenu Québec's transmission portal. Quebec has enacted a phased mandatory B2B e-invoicing/e-reporting regime (Revenu Québec's PEAM modernization initiative) scheduled to begin for large businesses in 2026 and broaden to smaller enterprises thereafter; API/EDI exchange with Revenu Québec will be required once the mandate applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under ETA Schedule VI Part V where (a) the supplier exports the bunker fuel/lubricants as ships' stores as part of the supply and retains prescribed evidence; or (b) the goods are supplied to a non-resident person for delivery to a destination outside Canada. Bunker fuel loaded at a Canadian port onto an oceangoing vessel for consumption during an international voyage is zero-rated as an export/ships' stores supply; lubricants and replenishment supplies similarly qualify if they form part of the vessel's stores for international use. Supplies taking place entirely outside Canadian territorial waters fall outside the GST/HST/QST net (no Canadian tax). Where fuel is sold for domestic (coastal) voyages, the standard 14.975% GST+QST applies unless a provincial rebate applies. The supplier must act with due diligence and retain contemporaneous evidence; CRA may otherwise assess the tax as collected but unremitted.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (Form B13A filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System, CERS) for goods exported from Canada with a value exceeding CAD 2,000
Ocean bill of lading (port-to-port or through B/L) evidencing delivery of the bunker fuel to the named vessel and its intended international voyage/destination

Inward remittance evidence (bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice or bank confirmation of receipt of export proceeds; Canadian banks do not issue a separate 'inward remittance certificate', so the banking record serves as the equivalent)
Bunker delivery note (BDN) and independent quantity survey document evidencing the marine fuel/lubricant quantity delivered to the vessel as ships' stores
Commercial invoice, sales contract, and INCOTERMS clause evidencing sale to the non-resident ship owner/charterer/operator

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central bank and fiscal agent; foreign exchange administration is otherwise governed by the Minister of Finance and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act and the Currency Act; anti-money-laundering surveillance sits with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and Quebec entities also face the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) for securities and payment-services matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current-account and capital-account transactions; Canada maintains no general exchange-control regime, no requirement to repatriate or convert export proceeds, and no restriction on capital inflows or outflows. Profit remittance is unrestricted; however, for a Quebec limited partnership (CA_LP), allocations of Canadian-source business income to non-resident limited partners are taxable under Part I of the Income Tax Act (Canada) via a T5013 partnership information return and corresponding non-resident T1/T2 filings, while only amounts characterized as interest, royalties, management fees, or certain deemed dividends attract Part XIII withholding at 25% (subject to treaty reduction). Non-resident investors must also comply with the Investment Canada Act notification if non-control acquisitions exceed prescribed asset thresholds (CAD 5 million in 2025 for trade-agreement WTO investors, updated annually); no restrictions exist on dividend or distribution repatriation by the LP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds from marine fuel bunkering; receipts may be held in CAD or foreign currency; however, the LP must report foreign-currency accounts on CRA Form T1135 when total foreign-specifie property exceeds CAD 100,000, and FINTRAC requires reporting of all cross-border electronic fund transfers (EFT) of CAD 10,000 or more, plus Large Virtual Currency Transaction Reports (LVCTR).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Desjardins Group (Federation des caisses Desjardins du Quebec)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-Low (restricted). A non-Canadian electronic money institution (EMI) cannot act as the primary treasury or settlement account for the Quebec LP unless it holds a FINTRAC Money Services Business (MSB) registration and, if it processes retail payment obligations in final settlement, a registration with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA). Quebec's Act respecting payment services (Loi concernant les services de paiement) further requires authorization to offer deposit or electronic-money services in Quebec. A structure using a licensed foreign EMI as a virtual-IBAN cost-optimization overlay on top of a Schedule I bank account is viable; using the EMI as the sole liquidity rail is not compliant for CAD-denominated clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is partially permitted: individual signatories may complete video-KYC if they hold valid Canadian or US government-issued ID, but the limited partnership itself requires a notarized extract from the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, the full partnership agreement, and a compliance interview with the general partner or an authorized officer. Canadian banks, guided by FINTRAC's Organizations and Legal Arrangements Identification Requirements, require the physical presence of at least one authorized representative (usually the general partner or a Canadian-resident attorney-in-fact) at a branch, or an attestation certified by a Canadian notary or licensed lawyer, plus proof of the authority to bind the LP. A foreign general partner can appoint a Canadian-based officer or counsel with a power of attorney endorsed by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque multi-tiered partnership chain with non-resident limited partners lacking disclosed ultimate beneficial ownership (25% or more).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Consolidated UBO chart from each entity; chain of certificates; extract from Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; notarized declaration of ownership; audited financial statements of each partner; CFO attestation of no nominee or bearer interests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) nexus detected in marine-fuel counterparties, ship owners, or supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions and PEP screening results from a reputable vendor (World-Check or equivalent); five-year address and employment history for each UBO; source-of-wealth report; corporate vetting file on major oil suppliers; negative news search; sworn affidavit confirming no sanctioned vessel or cargo (ISPS, MARPOL compliance).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk or FATF blacklist/grey-list jurisdiction funding of the LP's capital account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from funding accounts showing commercial origin; commercial contracts, invoices, and bill-of-lading; surveyor certificates and bunker delivery notes; sworn source-of-funds declaration; external legal opinion on adequacy of asset freeze compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive bunkering settlements inconsistent with the declared Medium-Risk Enhanced profile, or unexpected third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: P&I club insurance certificate; detailed settlement schedule with ship owners; bank reference letters; explanation of cash lifecycle; sanctions-screened sub-accounts; maintain a clear audit trail linking each payment to a named vessel and ISIN/IMO number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing FATCA/CRS self-certification or incorrect CRS classification of the flow-through LP.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed IRS Form W-8BEN-E or W-9 as applicable; CRA Form RC518 (CRS self-certification) and Form RC519 for entities; Canada-US intergovernmental agreement classification; Quebec financial statements disclosure; confirmation that the LP is a 'Financial Institution' category F for offshore bribery risk only if relevant, otherwise treated as a non-financial entity per CRS.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Funds are routed via SWIFT MT103 (with UETR and SWIFT gpi tracking) from the foreign parent or partners into the LP's capital escrow account at a Schedule I bank. Instruction must include the full legal name of the LP (as registered in Quebec), the 19-digit registration number from the Registraire des entreprises, and a purpose narrative 'Capital contribution to limited partnership' with a clear reference for the compliance record. For incoming EFTs over CAD 10,000 the beneficiary bank files the FINTRAC EFT report; ensure the remitter and beneficiary identifiers match KYC records. Use purpose code 'TRD' (trade) or 'CFO' (corporate finance operation) per SWIFT usage guidelines; no MT202 COVER is needed for a same-bank or single-currency transfer, but split payments (MT103 + MT202) require exact beneficiary naming to avoid rejection. The LP should verify that the funds do not originate from a FATF high-risk jurisdiction and, for inbound USD, use CHIPS or FEDWIRE to intermediate in USD then convert to CAD at the bank's spot rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for bunker fuel purchases and lubricant replenishment use (i) SWIFT MT103 with UETR for standard trade settlement; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit (UCP600) with MT700/MT707 series for high-value cargo purchases, payable at sight or deferred; (iii) standby letters of credit (ISP98) securing supply contracts and customs/tax guarantees; and (iv) domestic CAD payments cleared through Lynx (high-value) or ACSS (ACH) for smaller disbursements. For USD-denominated settlements, payments clear via CHIPS or FEDWIRE. Supporting documentation must include the commercial invoice, bunker delivery note (BDN), loading port quantity, independent surveyor certificate, bill of lading, and any required ISPS/MARPOL certificates. Since the LP is not a bank, any LC must be issued by a Canadian chartered bank in favor of the bunker supplier, with the LP as applicant under an approved credit facility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter FX forwards (ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank counterparty; credit support annex under Quebec civil law pledge).
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) but only for cross-currency exposure to non-convertible or emerging-market currencies where CAD/USD deliverability is absent.
FX swaps (FX swap) and cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for matched funding of USD receivables and CAD payables.
Vanilla FX options and barrier options (covered by ISDA/CSA and requiring OSFI-qualified counterparty approval).
Listed FX futures and options on a recognized Canadian exchange such as the Montreal Exchange (TMX Group) for liquid CAD/USD and CAD/EUR hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default notice followed by administrative strike-off; restoration requires court order and additional fees; late filing may trigger penalties under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficiary Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual declaration; any changes in beneficial ownership must be reported within 60 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Same as annual declaration; refusal to update may prevent issuance of certificates and lead to administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (6 months for partnerships with any non-resident partner)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of $40 per month per active partner (minimum $100, maximum $500); additional penalties upon demand; risk of loss of capacity to claim expenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (aligned with the federal T5013)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest and penalty on late-filed information return; a 10% late penalty on any unpaid provincial tax (if applicable), and an additional 10% if a penalty was previously charged; criminal prosecution for willful non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit for a Quebec limited partnership under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. An audit may be required by the partnership agreement, by a secured creditor, or if the partnership becomes a reporting issuer under securities laws.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); allocation of income must follow the partnership agreement and be reported under the Income Tax Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual declaration must confirm or update the list of ultimate beneficiaries, being any individual with 25% or more of the rights in the partnership's assets or profits or control over the general partner. Any change during the year must be filed with the enterprise registry within 60 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by law; voluntary review or audit market range: $5,000 – $15,000 USD

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% (combined federal 15.0% general corporate rate plus Quebec provincial rate of 11.5%, reflecting the 10% federal abatement for Quebec-based income; limited partnership itself is fiscally transparent so the effective rate applies at the partner level)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Limited partnership (LP) is pass-through; no LP-level tax. Partners are taxed on their allocable share. Qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partners may access the small business deduction (federal 9% and Quebec 3.2% on first CAD 500,000 active business income). Quebec refundable tax credits (e.g., C3i innovation, film and multimedia credits) may reduce effective provincial tax. Federal manufacturing and processing credits may apply to eligible activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 Summary and T5013 Supplementary Forms (Information Return for Partnership) filed through the Canada Revenue Agency's EFILE or Internet File Transfer. Quebec: Revenu Quebec Form TP-600 (Sociétés de personnes) filed electronically via clic SÉ@T.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013 must be filed by March 31 following the calendar year-end, or if the LP has a non-calendar fiscal period, the last day of the third month after the fiscal period end. TP-600 due by March 31 following the taxation year (or the last day of the third month after a non-December 31 fiscal period end). Partners file their own returns by their deadlines (April 30 for individuals; six months after corporate fiscal year-end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: LP legal name, business number (BN), fiscal period start/end, principal business activity (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide Canadian business number and designate an agent for service in Canada. Disclose each non-resident limited partner's name, country of residence, and any Canadian non-resident tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Partners' allocation of income or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Each partner's share of gross income, expenses, taxable income, and foreign-source income per the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate income only to the extent attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment. Attach schedule identifying non-resident limited partners and their allocation percentage under subsection 96(1).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Cost and capital allowances (CCA and eligible capital property)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation (CCA) claims, capital gains, and cumulative eligible capital deductions computed at the LP level.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners cannot claim CCA directly unless the LP carries on business through a permanent establishment in Canada; complete the applicable CCA schedule indicating the Quebec permanent establishment address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Foreign tax credits and non-resident withholding
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign taxes paid by the LP allocable to partners and any Part XIII tax withheld on payments (interest, royalties, management fees) to non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Part XIII withholding on any non-resident partner's non-business Canadian-source income; attach NR4 or RL-15 slips and Form NR301 if treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income allocation and provincial tax credits for losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident partner has a permanent establishment in Quebec, file TP-600 and make instalments; otherwise elect federal-only reporting under subsection 96(3) if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T5013: CAD 100 per partner per day capped at CAD 2,500 per partner. If more than 30 days late with unreported Part XIII withholding, an additional 5% penalty applies. Revenu Quebec: CAD 25 to CAD 2,500 plus CAD 10 per partner per day up to CAD 2,500. Interest accrues daily at prescribed CRA rates (currently 9% + 4% compounded daily for Quebec).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding on dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident partner/shareholder. Treaty-reduced rates generally 5% for a 10% voting shareholder or 15% for portfolio dividends under the Canada-US treaty and other Canadian DTAs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief: (1) obtain a valid foreign tax authority Certificate of Residence (Form NR301 or equivalent); (2) submit the form to the Canadian withholding agent before payment, or within two years after the calendar year of payment for a refund; (3) confirm beneficial ownership and meet any limitation-on-benefits provision; (4) file NR4 or a waiver under subsection 216(1) to reduce or refund Part XIII withheld amounts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 25% on royalties and interest. Treaty rates under Canada-US DTA: 0% for industrial property royalties; 10% for copyright royalties (15% for certain other IP); 0% for arm's-length interest; 15% for non-arm's-length or excessive interest. Quebec does not levy additional withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 (total controlled transactions requiring a local file and master file). CbCR threshold CAD 1,000,000,000 (consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada applies the economic substance doctrine through section 247 of the Income Tax Act, Quebec through section 1007 of the Taxation Act. A bunkering LP must show substantive presence (storage infrastructure, vessels, personnel, invoicing, risk management) in Quebec. A shell conduit without real substance will be denied treaty benefits and re-characterized under GAAR.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly underreporting bunker fuel sales, inflating expenses, or falsely allocating income to non-resident partners without a permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act subsection 239(1): fine of 50% to 100% of tax evaded plus imprisonment up to 2 years. Quebec Taxation Act section 1069: fine of 50% of evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 2 years. Civil gross negligence penalty under subsection 163(2): 50% of understated tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners personally liable for unremitted withholdings under subsection 227.1(1). Civil restitution orders, travel bans under tax enforcement provisions, and imprisonment for failure to deduct or remit Part XIII taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Quebec LP as a conduit without real bunkering operations; channeling dividends or interest to a zero-tax jurisdiction without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR reassessment: denial of treaty benefits; 25% Part XIII withholding on amounts paid; 25% gross negligence penalty; interest at prescribed rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Jeopardy orders freezing assets, travel bans, seizure of personal bank accounts, joint and several liability for withholding obligations, and possible extradition for tax crimes under mutual legal assistance treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct CDD on high-risk bunker fuel counterparties; unreported suspicious wire transfers or SWIFT payments; false invoicing to conceal beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA monetary penalties up to CAD 105,000 for individuals and CAD 525,000 for corporations/partnerships; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years for money laundering under Criminal Code section 462.31.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal prosecution for missing AML compliance program; civil forfeiture of personal assets; travel bans; imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 10 years for organized crime connection).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating bunkering facilities without required Quebec Certificate of Authorization or Transport Canada permits; fuel spills causing environmental damage and improper loss claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Quebec Environment Quality Act fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years for clandestine discharge; Transport Canada civil penalties up to CAD 250,000 plus cleanup costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for cleanup costs under Environment Quality Act unless due diligence proven; travel bans possible pending criminal trial; imprisonment for wilful spills.
